target_customer: Online marketplaces, e-commerce and fintech companies that need to stop fraud and abuse
problem: Rules based fraud tools were hard to maintain; Sift applies large scale machine learning across a shared network of events to score fraud risk.
business_model: B2B SaaS priced by usage and volume
product_category: Fraud prevention and digital trust and safety

founders.name: Jason Tan
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch March 2013 lists these employers and says he was Ballinger's college roommate. The Sift about page lists him as Founder and Executive Chairman.

founders.name: Brandon Ballinger
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by TechCrunch March 2013; the YC page lists only Jason Tan. One source says he has since left.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building real time machine learning across many customers' event streams with low latency was hard for a small team, helped by ex-Google engineers (TechCrunch March 2013).

defensibility.rationale: A cross-customer data network improves scores with scale and integrations are sticky; the company reports 40 plus patents.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Sift stayed independent, bought Chargeback and Keyless in 2021, and sold Keyless to Ping Identity on October 30, 2025 per a deal database.

market_need_then: TechCrunch March 2013 describes existing anti-fraud vendors as rule heavy and reports early testers including Airbnb, Uber, Listia and Affirm.

branding.domain_note: Moved from Sift Science to sift.com when the company dropped Science in January 2019; domain purchase not documented.

identity.logo: A new logo and brand identity were launched with the 2019 rebrand; the company has a public brand center
identity.visual_style: Streamlined, modern identity per the 2019 announcement
identity.voice_and_tone: Mission led: help everyone trust the Internet

rebrands.why: Company said it dropped Science and moved to a more streamlined, modern identity

brand_strength.rationale: Short evocative name known in fraud prevention, helped by the 2019 simplification, but no evidence of consumer pull.

outcome_analysis: Sift launched with ex-Google machine learning engineers and a strong investor group, raised Series A to D by 2018 (about $107M), and reached a reported $1B valuation in 2021. It acquired Chargeback and Keyless in 2021 and sold Keyless in 2025. No acquisition of Sift itself was found. Anonymous reviews mention layoffs but no verified reporting was found.
notes: The Series B date is 2014 per the YC blog URL title and a wiki mirror (April 2014); the Series C 2016 article was seen only in search results. The 2021 $50M Series E and $1B valuation rest on a single database (Multiples.vc, Seedtable repeats the round). CB Insights lists Sift as Acquired on 2025-10-30, but that date matches the Keyless divestiture, so no exit is recorded. Total raised conflicts ($107M press at 2018, $156M databases). The 2021 and Keyless acquisitions (Chargeback, Keyless) are noted here, not as rounds. No competitor was named in dated early sources: TechCrunch March 2013 says only a number of anti-fraud vendors, so the list is empty. Current CEO is Marc Friend per the Sift page; Marc Olesen was CEO in 2021. Correction: Series A investors set to Union Square Ventures (lead, 2013); the other names previously listed there (First Round, Y Combinator, angels) belong to the seed or the 5.5M total and are not confirmed for the A. Series B dated 2014-05 (May 14, 2014 per multiple outlets); sources differ on whether First Round also joined. The April 2021 Series E ($50M, over $1B valuation) was led by Insight Partners with Union Square Ventures and Stripes per the Insight announcement. The Series E-1 (25M, 2021-09, 1.84B post-money) rests on a single source (Forge, a secondary-market platform) and is unverified; Forge lists the April round at a different amount.
